chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Saʿd ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about the traveler to Makkah and elsewhere: is the salat of the two ʿIds, al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā, obligatory upon him? He said: Yes, except at Minā on the Day of Sacrifice.
So the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, not obligation and mandatory duty.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; an encouraged act that is not obligatory
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler whose legal duty is being discussed
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the prayer of the two ʿIds, ʿId al-Fiṭr and ʿId al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the location excepted in the report on the Day of Sacrifice
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: Is salat of ʿId al-Fiṭr and ʿId al-Aḍḥā obligatory for a traveler?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of the salat of the two ʿIds for a traveler. Although the report outwardly answers in the affirmative, the concluding statement clarifies that it is to be understood as recommendation rather than obligation. It thus contributes to the jurisprudential discussion on the dropping of ʿId prayer from the traveler.
